title: Consolidate ledger reconciler to handle interleaved proration and rate-limit credit adjustments
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Symptom: Customers and accounting observed interleaved invoice line items where late rate-limit credits and per-hour proration adjustments were assigned to conflicting hourly buckets in the Netsuite export. This causes duplicated or missing invoice lines, incorrect proration rounding, and downstream reconciliation failures. Root cause hypothesis: multiple reconciler passes (hourly usage rollup + late-adjustment backfills) use slightly different anchoring logic when converting timestamps into billing windows. When a rate-limit credit arrives late and triggers a backfill, existing invoice-line merging logic sometimes splits a proration delta across adjacent anchors, producing non-idempotent export signatures and duplicate lines in downstream Netsuite ingest.
acceptance_criteria: Hourly reconciler outputs deterministic, idempotent invoice-line keys for a given set of usage and credit events
Late-arriving rate-limit credits and proration adjustments are merged into existing invoice lines instead of creating duplicates
End-to-end sample of affected customer accounts shows zero net change in outstanding balance after reconciliation (i.e., no double credits or missing charges)
Export signatures include a checksum and anomaly flag when reconciliation makes a corrective change
Unit and integration tests cover DST boundary, multi-currency rounding, and cross-region clock skew cases
implementation_notes: Unify anchor logic: centralize time-to-billing-window mapping into billing/anchoring.v2 with deterministic bucketing rules (explicit UTC floor, plus plan-level offset), replace ad-hoc implementations in hourly rollup and late-adjustment jobs
Introduce invoice_line_fingerprint: stable 64-bit hash over (customer_id, plan_id, usage_bucket_ts, billing_unit_type, currency, commit_sequence) to produce idempotent line keys
On late adjustments, perform an atomic merge: lookup existing fingerprint and update quantity/amount, record a corrective_change record with before/after checksum
Add a reconciliation dry-run mode that emits candidate merges and anomaly flags but does not modify exports; expose via internal console route for ops review
Backfill strategy: run dry-run on last 21 days, surface top 100 affected customers, then run targeted corrective exports with fallbacks to manual approval
qa_plan: Create synthetic dataset with interleaved events (rate-limit credits, plan swaps, DST transitions) and assert reconciler idempotency over repeated runs
End-to-end test against a staging Netsuite export consumer to verify no duplicate lines are created
Manual validation: finance will sample 25 accounts pre/post change and confirm invoice totals and rounding behavior
Load test: ensure new anchoring and merge logic adds less than 10% CPU/time to current reconciler pipeline for 1M hourly buckets
rollout_and_mitigation: Deploy anchoring.v2 behind a feature flag; default to legacy behavior
Run reconciler in dry-run mode for 72 hours and compare anomaly rates versus baseline; if >1% regression, roll back flag
If corrective exports are required, queue them with per-customer throttling and rate-limit awareness to avoid sudden invoice churn
Provide ops playbook: how to revert an applied corrective export and how to annotate accounting tickets with corrective_change checksums

Estimated work split: 40% engineering (reconciler changes + tests), 30% QA/staging verification, 30% finance/ops coordination for corrective exports
